title: Accuracy of bedside tests against the exercise-test anaerobic threshold for triage to prehabilitation before major abdominal surgery
abstract: Objective: to validate pre-specified cut-offs of the 30-second sit-to-stand test and gait speed for a low anaerobic threshold. Design: consecutive-patient accuracy study with blinded testers. Primary outcome: sensitivity of sit-to-stand 10 or fewer. Results will be written after recruitment.
introduction: Exercise testing is too slow to triage every patient for prehabilitation before major abdominal surgery. Bedside tests are fast, but their published cut-offs were derived in their own data and never validated.
methods: Consecutive adults did both bedside tests at pre-assessment and exercise testing within two weeks, with testers blind to each other's results. Patients unable to complete exercise testing were classified by a pre-specified rule, and cut-offs were fixed before recruitment.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the flow of patients, cross-tables for each test, sensitivity and specificity with intervals, and results for patients aged 75 and over.
discussion: The discussion will compare validated accuracy with the published estimates and state whether bedside triage is acceptable for allocating places. It will consider the patients who could not complete either test.
limitations: This is a single centre, and blinding depends on the order of testing. The prevalence of the target condition may differ from the planning value.
conclusion: To be written after analysis. It will state whether the pre-specified cut-off meets the triage threshold.
